plan.title: Who gets a vote? · Editorial meeting
plan.intent: Create a role-play activity that simulates an editorial review meeting. Assign students as Story Author, First-time Reader, Evidence Checker, and Critical Editor. Have them examine how area, labels, and sequence convey the message, then write a shared critique.

tasks.title: Story Author
tasks.prompt: What message does the seven-frame story communicate? Explain how changing area supports that message.
tasks.handoff: Use the group’s initial reading in your role task. Bring your findings back to the shared critique.

tasks.title: First-time Reader
tasks.prompt: Compare the first and final frames. What does area represent? Name one step that needs a clearer explanation.
tasks.handoff: Use the group’s initial reading in your role task. Bring your findings back to the shared critique.

tasks.title: Evidence Checker
tasks.prompt: Check the dates and population groups. Why do the voting data and Senate election refer to different years?
tasks.handoff: Use the group’s initial reading in your role task. Bring your findings back to the shared critique.

tasks.title: Critical Editor
tasks.prompt: Which step supports the claim about a small voting population? State one claim the story cannot establish.
tasks.handoff: Use the group’s initial reading in your role task. Bring your findings back to the shared critique.

phases.title: Discuss together
phases.instruction: Compare the first and last frames. Record one initial group reading.

phases.title: Work by role
phases.instruction: Use the group’s initial reading. Complete your role task before opening peer work.

phases.title: Write together
phases.instruction: Bring all role findings together. Write one shared critique.

studio.editInstruction: Start with a group discussion of the first and last frames. Record one initial reading. Then let the four roles examine that reading on their own. Finally, bring their findings together to write one shared critique.

rules.title: Each learner makes a contribution
rules.expectation: Each learner saves one role contribution by the chosen checkpoint. A help request also prompts review.
rules.evidence: Saved role submissions; no claim about spoken participation.
rules.response: Visit the learner, clarify the task, or adjust their workload.
rules.nextTime: If one role is late in most teams, shrink that role’s task.

rules.title: Each learner distinguishes filtering from time
rules.expectation: Each learner identifies a population filter and explains the reading.
rules.evidence: A private multiple-choice answer and a short reason. An incorrect answer is flagged for review.
rules.response: Preview a frame comparison for this team, then assign a private follow-up.
rules.nextTime: Put the private question before the discussion.

rules.title: Peer questions receive a response
rules.expectation: Before submitting the shared critique, respond to each Reader question or explicitly record what remains unresolved.
rules.evidence: Teacher inspects the Reader log and shared critique, or asks the team. No automatic rubric score.
rules.response: Ask the Author or Checker to answer the unresolved question before revising.
rules.nextTime: Add “reply to a peer” as a step before shared writing.

rules.title: A learner asks for a different way to work
rules.expectation: Learners can request smaller steps or a written way to contribute.
rules.evidence: An explicit private request. Silence or inactivity is not a diagnosis.
rules.response: Review the request, then preview step-by-step support or a written exchange.
rules.nextTime: Start with individual writing before talk.

rules.title: Agreement includes a check of reasoning
rules.expectation: When all initial choices match, record a response to a contrasting claim and one linked peer check.
rules.evidence: All active team members saved the same private MCQ choice. Agreement alone is not a problem.
rules.response: Review reasons. Keep the activity, test the agreed claim, or add conceptual support.
rules.nextTime: Group learners by different first answers.

rules.title: Shared work has more than one author
rules.expectation: At least two members add to or edit the shared critique.
rules.evidence: Who saved each change to the shared critique. One member may be typing for the team, so ask before judging.
rules.response: Ask for one round of turns: each member adds a point before the team finishes.
rules.nextTime: Give each member a named section of the shared product.

rules.title: Any member can explain the team’s answer
rules.expectation: One member, picked at random when the critique is saved, explains the team’s decision and one reason in private.
rules.evidence: The picked member’s written explanation. The teacher reads it against the critique.
rules.response: Ask teammates to explain again, then pick another member.
rules.nextTime: Tell the class about the random pick at the start.

rules.title: Decisions have a second sign-off
rules.expectation: A member who did not save the critique reads it and signs off with one reason.
rules.evidence: Sign-offs on the current version of the shared critique. Editing the critique asks for a new sign-off.
rules.response: Remind the team that the critique needs a second reader before they finish.
rules.nextTime: Turn sign-off on from the start for ranking and table tasks.

rules.title: The team works together during shared stages
rules.expectation: During a shared stage the team edits its shared work or posts a one-line status.
rules.evidence: Times of shared edits and status lines. Speech is not recorded; the team may be talking.
rules.response: Visit the team, or add one round of turns.
rules.nextTime: Add a mid-stage status line to the activity.

rules.title: No learner stalls mid-stage
rules.expectation: Each learner saves some change during individual work until their role work is shared.
rules.evidence: The time of each learner’s last saved change. Reading and thinking leave no trace.
rules.response: Read the draft. Offer smaller steps to that learner and keep the same goal.
rules.nextTime: Start that task with a worked example.

rules.title: One step does not block many learners
rules.expectation: Most learners get past each step of the activity.
rules.evidence: Missing work at the checkpoint across the class, and requests for smaller steps.
rules.response: Clarify to the whole class and add time.
rules.nextTime: Rewrite that step. This is a design problem, not a learner problem.

rules.title: An early finish gets a depth check
rules.expectation: A team uses the stage to reason, not only to fill fields.
rules.evidence: The stage time left when the team first saved its work. Needs a live, timed stage.
rules.response: Pick a member to explain the answer. Strong answer: give an extension. Weak answer: reopen it.
rules.nextTime: Raise the task demand, or prepare an extension.

rules.title: No role is behind in most teams
rules.expectation: Roles finish their work at similar times.
rules.evidence: Which role had not shared work at the checkpoint, compared across teams.
rules.response: Add time, or move one sub-task to another role.
rules.nextTime: Rebalance the role briefs.

rules.title: A shared wrong answer goes to the teacher
rules.expectation: A team that shares one wrong first answer gets new information from the teacher, not more peer discussion.
rules.evidence: All private first answers in the team. Discussion among learners who share a wrong answer tends to confirm it.
rules.response: Explain, or add a contrasting case. Then ask a new private question.
rules.nextTime: Add the contrasting case to the material.

rules.title: A minority view gets a reasoned response
rules.expectation: The shared critique says why the team rejected another reading, or records it as unresolved.
rules.evidence: First choices that differ, an objection at sign-off, or a field that members keep overwriting, compared with the team’s “why not” note.
rules.response: Ask for three lines: reading A, reading B, and the evidence that would decide.
rules.nextTime: Put a rule for disagreement in the brief.

rules.title: Peer feedback names a concrete example
rules.expectation: Each piece of peer feedback points to one part of a peer’s work and gives a reason.
rules.evidence: Sign-off notes, claim checks and replies to peers: their length and whether they name a target. Quality still needs a teacher’s read.
rules.response: Ask for the example behind the judgment.
rules.nextTime: Make the target a required field.

rules.title: Each learner gives a private closing check
rules.expectation: At the end, each learner answers in private: Did you contribute? Was your work used? One thing to change.
rules.evidence: Private answers, seen by the teacher only. Read them beside the team’s record.
rules.response: Read it beside the team’s record. Talk to the learner in private.
rules.nextTime: Change roles or groups. Use the “one thing to change” answers in the next plan.

rules.title: Answers are written in the interface
rules.expectation: Learners write their answers in the answer fields.
rules.evidence: The length of each paste into an answer field. The pasted text is not stored.
rules.response: Ask the learner to explain the answer to a teammate.
rules.nextTime: Turn off paste in answer fields.

rules.title: Roles and teammates change across activities
rules.expectation: A learner does not hold the same role with the same teammates many times.
rules.evidence: Names, roles and teams from earlier activities in this library, matched by the name a learner enters.
rules.response: No change during class.
rules.nextTime: Rotate roles, regroup, or run a shorter version.

rules.title: Everyone has a chance to contribute
rules.expectation: Every learner can share an idea or ask for help.
rules.evidence: Teacher observation or a private help request. Speech is not recorded.
rules.response: Offer a written exchange, clarify a role, or visit the team.
rules.nextTime: Start with individual writing before talk.

b06be2863b.discuss:task-1793064281445-0:
A small slice of voters helps decide Senate control. — The shrinking map makes the narrowing electorate visible.
 —

1eecbcefdc.discuss:task-1793064281445-1: Frame 1: The smaller map could be mistaken for population falling over time. Which label rules that out?

f556e644bd.discuss:task-1793064281445-2: The maps show population falling over time. — The population unit is constant. Labels filter who is counted; this is not a sequence of dates.

ff63712d82.discuss:task-1793064281445-3: Keep the narrowing-electorate claim. Clarify that area represents people and filters change who is counted.

observations.text: The smaller map could be mistaken for population falling over time. Which label rules that out?

checks.statement: The maps show population falling over time.
checks.reason: The population unit is constant. Labels filter who is counted; this is not a sequence of dates.

ff63712d82.reflection: Keep the narrowing-electorate claim. Clarify that area represents people and filters change who is counted.

opening.text: The maps narrow from all Americans to a small group of voters. Smaller area means fewer people are included, not that the population falls over time.

initial.reason: The later frames look smaller, so I read them as a population decline.

followup.reason: The label changes who is counted. A state can shrink after filtering even if its total population is unchanged.

initial.reason: I thought the sequence showed the population dropping.

followup.reason: Each frame filters the set of people. The area changes without requiring a population decline.

initial.reason: The labels narrow the population groups; these are not later dates.
